upshift.tooltip.scale: The world renders at this percentage of the window on each axis, then gets upscaled. 67%% of 1920x1080 is 1286x723.
upshift.tooltip.sharpness: 0.00 is a single bilinear tap: the cheapest an upscale gets. Above 0 the five-tap sharpening kernel runs, 0.20 is crisp, 1.00 is subtle.
upshift.tooltip.full_easu: Use FidelityFX EASU instead of the cheap resize. Sixteen texture taps per pixel: better edges, several milliseconds more expensive on older cards.
upshift.tooltip.auto_fallback: When the selected upscaler cannot run, step down to the next one that can instead of turning scaling off.
upshift.tooltip.experimental: Offer every backend the device reports, including ones the vendor hides behind a model check. Off only skips paths the driver itself flags as unstable.
upshift.tooltip.overlay: Performance panel: frame rate, frame time, the slowest one percent, processor and graphics load, temperatures, clocks, memory, the resolutions in use and a frame-time graph.
upshift.tooltip.report: Print what this machine can run, and why, to chat and the log.
upshift.tooltip.frame_gen: The built-in generator presents extra predicted frames between the frames the game renders, so the display sees more images than the renderer produces. Each extra frame is the last finished image warped by the camera motion measured between the two previous poses; it needs no depth buffer, no native runtime and works on both backends. It only runs while the camera can move (no open screen) and backs off when the display has no room for extra frames. Vendor generators need their native runtime.
upshift.tooltip.dynamic: Moves the internal resolution up and down to hold the target frame rate. Steps are small and at most twice a second.
upshift.tooltip.target_fps: What the automatic resolution aims for. Set it to your refresh rate; above it, the controller just pushes the scale to 100%.
upshift.tooltip.quality: The presets the selected upscaler publishes, with the internal resolution each one implies: FSR 1 goes from ultra quality (77%) to performance (50%), temporal families also offer ultra performance (33%).
upshift.tooltip.fg_multiplier: How many frames are presented for every rendered frame: 1x presents only the real frame, 2x adds one predicted frame, 3x adds two, 4x adds three. On a display that cannot show that many images the extra presents are blocked by the refresh, so raise this only when the rendered frame rate is well below the refresh rate.
upshift.tooltip.fg_force: Normally the multiplier is capped by the measured gap between real frames, so a scene that already fills the display never pays for frames it cannot show. Turn this on to present exactly the selected number of frames regardless of the refresh rate.
upshift.tooltip.menu_boost: A screen cannot move the camera, so the world image behind it is still valid: three frames in four are re-resolved from it instead of drawing the level again, and the background blur is turned off. Screens then run at the rate the screen costs. One frame in four is still drawn, so water, mobs and particles keep moving.
upshift.tooltip.entity_cull: Entities farther than this many blocks are not extracted or submitted at all. The vanilla limit depends on render distance and can reach 160 blocks; 0 keeps the vanilla behaviour.
upshift.tooltip.cull_invisible: Skip invisible non-player mobs entirely once they are outside eight blocks. Armour and held items of invisible players are still drawn, so this cannot be used to spot them. Off by default.
upshift.tooltip.particle_limit: Caps how many particles the client creates per tick, and drops particles past the distance below. Vanilla already drops everything past 32 blocks unless the spawn is forced.
upshift.tooltip.particle_distance: Particles spawned farther than this from the camera are ignored. 32 matches vanilla for normal spawns; lowering it helps with big explosions and farms.
upshift.tooltip.particle_budget: The most particles that may be created in a single tick. When the budget is used up, further spawns are dropped until the next tick. 1500 is high enough to keep ordinary scenes intact.
upshift.tooltip.block_entity_cull: Chests, signs, banners, beacons and other block entities farther than this are never extracted. Their vanilla renderers stop at 64 blocks by default, while some (beacons, conduits) reach 256; 0 keeps the vanilla limits.
upshift.tooltip.freeze_animations: Lava, water, fire and other animated textures stop advancing while the Minecraft window is not focused. Nothing is visible at that point anyway, so this only saves work.
upshift.tooltip.animation_skip: How often animated textures are advanced. Every frame is vanilla; every second frame halves the animation cost at high frame rates, at the price of slightly slower-looking lava and fire.
upshift.tooltip.cache_text: Reuses the laid-out form of repeated HUD strings (item counts, scoreboard, debug screen, overlays) and their widths instead of rebuilding them every frame. Turn off if a mod produces text that changes without changing its string.
upshift.tooltip.throttle_ai: On the integrated server (singleplayer and LAN), mobs farther than the distance below from every player skip their sensing tick and only run the cheap goal pass on most ticks. They keep moving. A dedicated server is unaffected because this is a client mod.
upshift.tooltip.ai_distance: Mobs beyond this many blocks from every player are throttled. Mobs closer to any player keep their full AI. 0 turns throttling off.
upshift.tooltip.ai_interval: How often distant mobs run a full AI tick. Every 4 ticks is the default: sensing and the goal scan run once, the cheap running-goal pass runs on the others. Higher values save more on big farms but make distant mobs react more slowly.
upshift.tooltip.animation_whitelist: Sprites that should always animate, even when animation freezing is active. One per line, supports wildcards: namespace:path, namespace:*, *:path, or * for all. Opens the config file for editing.
upshift.tooltip.sharpening_only: Run only the RCAS sharpening pass at 100% internal resolution. Disabled automatically when internal scale is below 100%.
upshift.tooltip.preset.balanced: Default: 67% internal, TAAU, 60 FPS target, vanilla particles. Good starting point.
upshift.tooltip.preset.cpu_first: CPU-bound systems: 75% internal, single-pass FSR 1, fewer particles/entities. Best when CPU is the bottleneck.
upshift.tooltip.preset.gpu_first: GPU-bound / high refresh: 50% internal, RCAS sharpen, 120 FPS target. Best when GPU is the bottleneck.
upshift.tooltip.preset.integrated: Integrated graphics / low-end: 45% internal, single-pass FSR 1, fewer entities/particles, 45 FPS target.
upshift.tooltip.anr_download: Downloads the official Apex Neural Rendering frame generation package (anr-fg-*-full.zip) from GitHub. You will be asked to confirm before anything is downloaded; the archive is verified with SHA-256 before it is unpacked. After the package is staged, the Vulkan layer will be installed automatically.
upshift.tooltip.anr_folder: Folder holding the staged ANR FG package (%s).
upshift.tooltip.anr_install_layer: Installs the ANR FG Vulkan implicit layer for the detected launcher (javaw.exe). Requires a game restart to take effect.
upshift.tooltip.anr_layer_active: The ANR FG Vulkan layer is installed and active. Restart the game if you just enabled it.
upshift.tooltip.anr_uninstall: Removes the ANR FG Vulkan implicit layer. The package files remain on disk for re-installation.
upshift.anr.consent.title: Download third-party native code?
upshift.anr.consent.message: Upshift will download the official ANR FG package from GitHub (apex-compute/ANR). It contains native DLLs and shaders that run on your GPU. The archive is verified with SHA-256 before it is unpacked. A Vulkan implicit layer will be installed in %APPDATA%/vulkan/implicit_layer.d/ for the detected javaw.exe. No admin rights required. Requires a game restart to take effect.
upshift.anr.done: ANR FG Vulkan layer installed at %s. Restart the game to activate it.
upshift.anr.uninstalled: ANR FG Vulkan layer uninstalled. Restart the game to deactivate it.
